title: Pressure-induced double-dome superconductivity in doped kagome metal Cs(V0.86Ta0.14)3Sb5 without charge density wave
authors: Haochen Sun, Jing Wang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Shiyan Li
abstract: The vanadium-based kagome superconductor CsV$_3$Sb$_5$ exhibits an intricate interplay between charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity (SC). Substituting Ta for V will suppress the CDW order and enhance superconductivity. Here, we report a high-pressure study up to 48 GPa on Ta-doped Cs(V$_{0.86}$Ta$_{0.14}$)$_3$Sb$_5$ with enhanced $T_\mathrm{c}$ around 5.29 K and without CDW order. At low pressures, unlike the characteristic $``$M-shaped" temperature-pressure phase diagram of the pristine CsV$_3$Sb$_5$, the Ta-doped compound exhibits a distinct non-monotonic evolution. Initially, $T_\mathrm{c}$ drops slightly from 5.29 K at ambient pressure to 4.90 K at 0.33 GPa, before increasing to a maximum of 5.70 K at 0.61 GPa. Upon further compression, $T_\mathrm{c}$ decreases continuously to 0.98 K at 12.3 GPa. At higher pressures, $T_\mathrm{c}$ rises again, reaching 4.46 K at 47.7 GPa. This evolution of $T_\mathrm{c}$ establishes two superconducting domes under pressure, which are similar to those in CsV$_3$Sb$_5$. Our results demonstrate that pressure-induced double-dome superconductivity is intrinsic to these V-based kagome superconductors, even in the absence of long-range CDW order.
summary: This work reports on high-pressure studies of the doped kagome superconductor Cs(V0.86Ta0.14)3Sb5, which lacks long-range CDW order. The key finding is the observation of a double-dome superconducting phase diagram under pressure. This demonstrates that the double-dome superconductivity is an intrinsic property of this class of materials, independent of the CDW state.
main_problem: The study investigates the persistence and nature of pressure-induced double-dome superconductivity in a doped kagome metal, specifically when the long-range Charge Density Wave (CDW) order is suppressed.
main_result: The Ta-doped compound exhibits a clear double-dome superconducting phase diagram under pressure, demonstrating that this feature is intrinsic to V-based kagome superconductors even without CDW order.
method: High-pressure electrical resistance measurements were performed up to 48 GPa using a diamond anvil cell, complemented by magnetization measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is the vanadium-based kagome superconductor Cs(V0.86Ta0.14)3Sb5. The research explores the interplay between superconductivity and charge order in this highly correlated electronic material.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), $T-P$ phase diagram, and the presence/absence of CDW resistivity anomalies.
important_parameters: Pressure range up to 48 GPa; doping level (Ta substitution for V); ambient pressure $T_c$ ($\approx 5.29 	ext{ K}$).
main_assumptions: The authors hypothesize that the second superconducting dome is driven by a pressure-induced Fermi surface Lifshitz transition.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the non-monotonic evolution of $T_c$ under pressure, clearly establishing the double-dome structure up to 47.7 GPa, while confirming the absence of a CDW anomaly.
paper_structure: The paper presents measurements showing the initial non-monotonic $T_c$ evolution at low pressure, followed by the demonstration of the high-pressure double-dome superconductivity, concluding that this feature is robust despite CDW suppression.
why_interesting: The study provides experimental evidence of unconventional superconductivity mechanisms (double-dome structure) in a strongly correlated system, offering insights into how electronic instabilities (like CDW) influence pairing symmetry and dome formation.
